name: US 5th Fleet (NAVCENT)
mission: Persian Gulf maritime security, Strait of Hormuz freedom of navigation, counter-piracy and counter-smuggling operations
description: Headquartered at Naval Support Activity Bahrain, US 5th Fleet is responsible for approximately 2.5 million square miles of maritime area covering the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, Arabian Sea, and Red Sea. It serves as the primary naval deterrent ensuring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of global oil transits daily.
vessels: ~30 ships including carrier strike group, amphibious ready group, destroyers, and patrol craft

name: US 6th Fleet (Naval Forces Europe)
mission: Mediterranean Sea security, NATO southern flank, Suez Canal western approach, support to European and African operations
description: Headquartered in Naples, Italy, US 6th Fleet operates across the Mediterranean Sea and Black Sea approaches. It provides naval power projection for NATO's southern flank and ensures security of the western approaches to the Suez Canal, a critical link for IMEC and BRI maritime routes connecting Europe to Asia.
vessels: Rotational force of ~40 ships including forward-deployed destroyers at Rota, Spain (FDNF-E), command ship USS Mount Whitney

name: US 7th Fleet (Western Pacific)
mission: Western Pacific and Indian Ocean security, freedom of navigation in South China Sea, Malacca Strait oversight
description: The largest forward-deployed US fleet, 7th Fleet operates from the International Date Line to the India-Pakistan border. Headquartered at Yokosuka, Japan, it maintains persistent presence in the South China Sea and conducts regular freedom of navigation operations (FONOPs) challenging excessive Chinese maritime claims. Its area of responsibility covers the critical Malacca Strait chokepoint.
vessels: 50-70 ships including carrier strike group (USS George Washington (replaced USS Ronald Reagan in 2024)), forward-deployed amphibious ships, cruisers, destroyers

name: USS Dwight D. Eisenhower Carrier Strike Group
mission: Red Sea maritime security, deterrence against Houthi anti-shipping attacks, protection of commercial shipping through Bab el-Mandeb
description: Deployed to the Red Sea in late 2023 through mid-2024, the Eisenhower CSG conducted sustained combat operations against Houthi forces in Yemen who were attacking commercial shipping transiting the Bab el-Mandeb strait. The strike group launched hundreds of defensive and offensive strikes, marking the most intense naval combat operations for the US Navy since World War II. The Eisenhower returned to Norfolk in July 2024 after a record 9-month deployment.
vessels: CVN-69 USS Eisenhower, cruiser USS Philippine Sea, destroyers USS Gravely and USS Mason, carrier air wing

name: USS Gerald R. Ford Carrier Strike Group
mission: Eastern Mediterranean deterrence, support to Israel operations, power projection in Levant Basin
description: The USS Gerald Ford, the Navy's newest supercarrier, was rapidly deployed to the Eastern Mediterranean in October 2023 following the Hamas attack on Israel. The strike group provided deterrence against regional escalation, particularly aimed at preventing Hezbollah and Iranian involvement. It operated in close coordination with 6th Fleet assets and served as a visible demonstration of US commitment to IMEC corridor security. The Ford returned to Norfolk in January 2024 after its combat deployment.
vessels: CVN-78 USS Gerald R. Ford, cruiser USS Normandy, destroyers USS Thomas Hudner, USS Ramage, USS Carney, carrier air wing

name: PLA Navy Support Base Djibouti
mission: Indian Ocean logistics hub, anti-piracy operations, protection of BRI maritime routes, power projection into Horn of Africa
description: China's first overseas military installation, the PLA Support Base in Djibouti sits at the strategic Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint where the Red Sea meets the Gulf of Aden. Officially designated for logistical support and anti-piracy, it serves as a key node for protecting BRI maritime shipping lanes through the Indian Ocean. The base has been significantly expanded since its opening, with a pier capable of hosting aircraft carriers.
vessels: Rotational deployments of 1-2 warships, supply vessels, marine garrison of ~400-2,000 personnel (estimates vary)

name: PLA Navy Southern Theater Fleet
mission: South China Sea control, Malacca Strait western approach, protection of maritime BRI routes, Taiwan contingency
description: The PLA Navy's Southern Theater Fleet is China's largest and most capable fleet, responsible for the South China Sea and approaches to the Malacca Strait. Operating from Zhanjiang and island bases across the Spratly and Paracel chains, it enforces China's nine-dash line claims and protects the maritime BRI corridor from the Strait of Malacca through the South China Sea to Chinese ports. Rapid modernization has added carriers, Type 055 destroyers, and nuclear submarines.
vessels: Major surface combatants including Type 055 destroyers, Type 054A frigates, diesel and nuclear submarines, carrier Shandong

name: Russian Black Sea Fleet
mission: Black Sea control, Bosphorus Strait access, eastern Mediterranean power projection via Tartus
description: Historically based at Sevastopol, Crimea, the Black Sea Fleet has suffered significant losses from Ukrainian strikes since 2022 and has partially relocated to Novorossiysk. Despite attrition, it remains Russia's gateway to the Mediterranean via the Turkish Straits (governed by the Montreux Convention). The fleet's diminished capacity has reduced Russian ability to contest the eastern Mediterranean and threatens the viability of its Tartus naval facility in Syria.
vessels: Diminished force after Ukraine war losses; frigates, patrol ships, submarines, landing ships. Lost flagship Moskva in April 2022

name: Russian Mediterranean Squadron (Tartus)
mission: Eastern Mediterranean presence, support to Syrian government, counter to NATO southern flank
description: Russia's permanent Mediterranean task force operates from the Tartus naval facility in Syria, Russia's only naval base outside the former Soviet Union. Reconstituted in 2013, the squadron provides Russia with power projection into the eastern Mediterranean, potentially contesting IMEC corridor routes. However, the fall of the Assad regime in late 2024 has placed the future of the Tartus base in serious doubt, potentially ending Russia's Mediterranean naval presence.
vessels: Rotational force typically including 5-10 warships, often drawn from Northern and Baltic Fleets to supplement depleted Black Sea Fleet

name: Indian Navy Western Fleet
mission: Arabian Sea security, Strait of Hormuz western approach, protection of Indian Ocean sea lanes, IMEC eastern anchor
description: India's Western Naval Command headquartered at Mumbai operates across the Arabian Sea, the western Indian Ocean, and approaches to the Strait of Hormuz. As India positions itself as a key IMEC corridor partner, the Western Fleet provides security for the maritime leg connecting Indian ports to the Gulf states. India's expanding carrier capability (INS Vikrant) and new base at Karwar strengthen its ability to secure these trade routes.
vessels: Aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya, destroyers, frigates, submarines, patrol aircraft. INS Vikrant available from Eastern Fleet

name: Indian Navy Eastern Fleet
mission: Bay of Bengal security, Malacca Strait western approach, Andaman and Nicobar Islands patrol, counter to Chinese Indian Ocean presence
description: India's Eastern Naval Command at Visakhapatnam, with forward positions at the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (just 150km from the Malacca Strait entrance), monitors Chinese naval expansion in the Indian Ocean. The tri-service command at the Andaman Islands gives India a strategic position to observe or interdict traffic through the Malacca Strait, a chokepoint through which 80% of China's oil imports transit.
vessels: Aircraft carrier INS Vikrant, destroyers, frigates, corvettes, submarines. Andaman & Nicobar Command forward-deployed assets

name: Combined Maritime Forces (CMF)
mission: Multinational maritime security across Middle Eastern waters, counter-piracy, counter-smuggling, freedom of navigation
description: Combined Maritime Forces is the world's largest multinational naval partnership, comprising 44 nations. Headquartered alongside US 5th Fleet in Bahrain, CMF operates three combined task forces: CTF-150 (maritime security), CTF-151 (counter-piracy), and CTF-152 (Arabian Gulf security). CMF patrols cover the critical corridor from the Suez Canal through the Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb, Gulf of Aden, Arabian Sea, and Persian Gulf — the entire western leg of both IMEC and BRI maritime routes.
vessels: Contributed warships from 44 partner nations, typically 15-20 vessels on patrol at any time

name: Operation Prosperity Guardian
mission: Protection of commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden from Houthi attacks targeting vessels transiting Bab el-Mandeb
description: Launched in December 2023 under US leadership, Operation Prosperity Guardian was formed in response to Houthi attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb strait. The Houthi campaign — declared in solidarity with Gaza — caused a 70% drop in Suez Canal traffic as shipping diverted around the Cape of Good Hope, directly threatening both IMEC and BRI maritime corridors. The operation involves naval escorts and strikes against Houthi launch sites in Yemen.
vessels: US, UK, Bahrain, Canada, France, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Seychelles, and Spain contributing destroyers, frigates, and patrol aircraft

name: Royal Navy East of Suez Presence
home_port: UK Naval Support Facility, Duqm, Oman / UKMCC Bahrain
mission: Persian Gulf patrol, Red Sea escort, protection of British trade routes east of Suez, support to Gulf allies
description: The UK's return to a permanent east-of-Suez naval presence, centered on the new naval support facility at Duqm, Oman, and the UK Maritime Component Command in Bahrain. The Royal Navy maintains 4-6 vessels in the Gulf region permanently, including mine countermeasure vessels and patrol ships. The UK Joint Logistics Support Base at Duqm provides a strategic facility outside the Strait of Hormuz, ensuring operational resilience if the strait is contested.
vessels: 2 permanently forward-deployed patrol ships (HMS Lancaster-class), mine countermeasure vessels, periodic destroyer/frigate deployments, RFA support ships

name: French Forces in the Southern Indian Ocean (FAZSOI)
mission: Indian Ocean maritime surveillance, Mozambique Channel patrol, anti-piracy, Djibouti-based Red Sea operations
description: France maintains the largest permanent military presence of any European nation in the Indian Ocean, split between Reunion Island (FAZSOI) and Djibouti (Forces Francaises a Djibouti). The Djibouti base, hosting ~1,500 troops and naval assets, sits directly on the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint. France's Indian Ocean territories (Reunion, Mayotte, Scattered Islands) give it sovereign EEZ covering vast ocean areas. French frigates regularly patrol the Mozambique Channel, a key BRI alternative route if Suez is blocked.
vessels: 2-3 frigates/corvettes, patrol vessels, maritime patrol aircraft (Falcon 50, Atlantique 2), amphibious ship rotational
